name: Syriac Fathers and Doctors (collective)
dom: asceticism; biblical exegesis; liturgical poetry; mysticism
note: Collective hub for the Aramaic-speaking Fathers, poets and theologians of West and East Syriac Christianity; well attested across Brock and Baum-Winkler.

name: Ephrem the Syrian
dom: liturgical poetry; symbolic theology; anti-heresy hymnody
note: Deacon of Nisibis and Edessa (c.306-373), 'Harp of the Spirit', greatest Syriac hymnographer; doctor of the universal church. Attested by his Madrashe and Brock's study.

name: Aphrahat the Persian Sage
note: Early-4th-c. Persian author of the 23 Demonstrations, earliest major Syriac theologian, writing under Sasanian rule. Attested by his Demonstrations and Baum-Winkler.

name: Isaac of Nineveh (Isaac the Syrian)
note: 7th-c. East Syriac bishop of Nineveh and hermit whose Ascetical Homilies on mercy and prayer were read across Orthodox monasticism. Attested by his homilies and Baum-Winkler.

name: Jacob of Serugh
note: West Syriac bishop (c.451-521), 'Flute of the Holy Spirit', author of hundreds of metrical verse homilies. Attested by his memre and Brock.

name: Narsai
dom: verse homily; biblical exegesis; theological education
note: 5th-c. East Syriac poet-theologian, 'Harp of the Spirit' of the Church of the East, head of the School of Nisibis. Attested by his metrical homilies and Baum-Winkler.

name: Babai the Great
note: East Syriac monk-theologian (c.551-628) who systematized Church-of-the-East dyophysite christology in his Book of the Union and reformed its monasteries. Attested by Baum-Winkler.

name: Bar Hebraeus (Gregory Abu al-Faraj)
note: 13th-c. West Syriac (Syriac Orthodox) maphrian, polymath and chronicler, last great classical Syriac author. Attested by his Chronicle and Baum-Winkler.

name: John of Ephesus
note: 6th-c. West Syriac (Miaphysite) bishop and historian, author of the Ecclesiastical History and Lives of the Eastern Saints. Attested by his historical works and Baum-Winkler.

name: Philoxenus of Mabbug
dom: miaphysite theology; ascetic teaching; scripture revision
note: West Syriac bishop (c.440-523), leading Miaphysite theologian and ascetic writer, sponsor of the Philoxenian Syriac New Testament. Attested by his discourses and Baum-Winkler.

name: Bardaisan of Edessa
note: Early Edessene Christian philosopher (154-222), author/subject of the Book of the Laws of Countries; later judged heterodox for astral-cosmological views. Foundational but contested figure; attested by Brock and the Dialogue.

name: Addai (Thaddeus of Edessa)
dom: apostolic mission; foundation of Edessan church
note: Apostle-evangelist of Edessa in the Abgar legend (Doctrine of Addai), traditional founder of Syriac Christianity. Legendary-traditional attestation via the Doctrine of Addai, cited in Baum-Winkler.
